faults.quote: Most Pro customers have a demo with a salesperson first, while Starter customers sign up online on their own.
faults.why: The candidate asked for the split of Starter sign-ups by source (paid versus organic). The interviewer released the sign-up channel line, which does not answer that, and did not say it lacks a paid/organic split.

faults.quote: With that, and the exhibit on your screen, what is Starter's total value per sign-up against its acquisition cost
faults.why: The candidate misread Pro's cost to serve as $22 (exhibit-1 says $20), giving a $78 margin and a $3,900 Pro LTV instead of $4,000. This flowed into the $780 upgrade value, which should be $800. No flat correction ever came.
At t7 the candidate said "you had it at $288" for Starter CAC; exhibit-1 says $300. The interviewer never corrected it, and $288 was carried through every ratio and the final recommendation.

faults.quote: Starter monthly cancellation rate is about 5%, not 4%.
faults.why: After probing the $28 margin, the candidate repeated that "the exhibit lists Starter's cost to serve at $12" (it is $10). The interviewer moved on to the churn correction and never corrected the $12, so the $28 margin and the $48 margin at $60 stood.

faults.quote: As the exhibit shows: New customers per month were 500 Pro in 2024, before Starter launched, and 350 Pro plus 1,000 Starter — 1,350 in total — from January 2025 to June 2026.
faults.why: The candidate asked whether Pro sign-ups were already trending down through 2024. The interviewer restated the exhibit line already on screen, which gives no within-2024 trend, and gave no refusal.

faults.quote: Now, an exhibit: Starter price test — New customers per month (eight-week test, August–September 2026). What do you take from this exhibit?
faults.why: The candidate stated wants for held data: whether Pro demo requests fell (why_pro_fell answers this), the profile of who buys each plan (buyer_profile), and competitor activity. The interviewer gave no release, refusal or deferral and moved straight to the next exhibit.

faults.quote: Right, a per-sign-up breakeven with a volume caveat.
faults.why: "Right" reads as approving the candidate's 10% breakeven, which is wrong (it should be 12.5%). The correction only came two turns later.

faults.quote: Of all the risks to your recommendation to keep Starter and move it to $60, which one is the biggest, and what would you do to guard against it?
faults.why: The candidate had already given risks and next steps (mitigation) in the t25 recommendation, so the risk question is largely re-asked.

faults.quote: Only a little time left — what's your bottom-line recommendation, and what's the biggest risk to it?
faults.why: The recommendation was given at t25. The biggest risk and its guard were given at t29 and refined at t31, the turn just before, yet both were asked again.
